text: Diagnostic prediction REFUTED as scored (E0003, local-full): mean logit diff 0.31 (std 2.68), accuracy 2/12. But the test did not measure what I intended: the answer labels I passed explicitly were permuted across prompts before scoring (prompt 0 was scored against ' Robert', which I supplied for prompt 10; prompt 1 against ' Steve', supplied for prompt 11; etc.). So in this investigation the lab scores every metric against labels that are shuffled relative to the prompts, for the built-in dataset (E0002) and for explicit labels (E0003) alike. I therefore cannot separate 'model has no IOI preference' from 'labels misaligned' with a scored metric. Unscored observation only: in all 8 example predictions printed (4 in E0002, 4 in E0003) the model's top-1 token is the non-repeated name in the prompt. That is anecdotal (n=8, no pre-registered metric) and supports no mechanism claim.

STOP after 3 experiments. With the labels this investigation provides, the model is at chance on the task (E0002: logit diff -0.016, accuracy 0.016; E0003: 0.31, 0.17). Any patching, ablation or attribution run would be optimising a logit difference between two names unrelated to the prompt, so any 'circuit' found would be noise. No mechanism search, no predict() code, no verify_hypothesis. Report as: no behaviour to explain under the provided labels; label/prompt misalignment flagged.
